4_map_sketch.total_area_of_operations: 4.0-mile radius centered at Intracoastal Waterway Mile Marker 245
4_map_sketch.incident_site_area: Confluence of the Intracoastal Waterway and Cypress Bayou

4_map_sketch.threatened_areas: Grand Cypress Mangrove Sanctuary 2.0 miles south-southeast; Delta Commercial Oyster Leases 3.5 miles down-river

4_map_sketch.impacted_shorelines: 1.5 miles south along the eastern bank of Cypress Bayou

5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.situation_summary: Tugboat towing two loaded asphalt barges collided with an anchored commercial tanker at 13:50 hours, rupturing Cargo Tank #2 starboard and releasing heavy fuel oil.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.health_and_safety_hazards: Hydrogen sulfide gas accumulation, hydrocarbon inhalation, direct dermal exposure, slip-and-fall hazards on oily/muddy surfaces, responder heat exhaustion in 91°F heat, and water drowning risks.
5_situation_summary_health_safety_briefi.necessary_measures: Establishment of a 1,000-foot Maritime Safety Zone, mandatory Level C PPE with half-mask organic vapor respirators and PFDs for over-water personnel, continuous H2S/PID air monitoring, mandatory work-rest hydration cycles, and vessel-based decontamination station.

7_current_and_planned_objectives: Complete primary deflection boom deployment across the mouth of Cypress Bayou by 16:30 hours.
Secure mechanical patching or product transfer (lightering) of Cargo Tank #2 by 18:00 hours.
Deploy skimming vessels to recover free-floating surface product before nightfall at 19:30 hours.
Establish a full Joint Information Center to handle media inquiries by 20:00 hours.

8_current_and_planned_actions_strategies.actions: Coast Guard Station Cypress Bend dispatched Sector Patrol Craft and issued a Notice to Mariners closing the waterway.
Captain M. Thorne established Incident Command and deployed first-responder skimmer boats.
Port Authority Hazmat Teams completed initial safety sweeps and confirmed zero structural fire threats.
Marine salvage engineers boarded the barge to inspect damage and prep transfer pumps.
Drop 2,000 feet of hard boom across the mangrove inlet.
Initiate lightering operations to pump fuel out of the damaged tank.
Deploy an evening drone overflight to track thermal slick drift patterns.

incident_commanders: Director D. Sterling (State Department of Environmental Quality)
H. Vance (Cypress Towing Co., Responsible Party)

10_resource_summary.notes: Enforcing maritime safety zone and conducting gas monitoring.
Actively skimming free surface product around the barge stern.
Providing stabilizing push-support and powering transfer pumps.
Collecting downstream water samples and turbidity readings.
En route with 3,000 feet of ocean containment boom and heavy skimmers.
En route to set up an oily bird stabilization and staging facility.
